items.article: CarJet enables users to compare costs on hiring a car abroad to find a deal that suits their budget and preferences Booking a hire car should be one of the simplest parts of planning a trip. However, for many travellers, the price they see online and the price they pay at the desk turn out to be very different things once costs like fuel charges, security deposits, insurance upgrades and location fees are factored in. Car hire comparison site CarJet aims to help travellers avoid these nasty surprises - bringing together offers from both local and international hire companies in one place and showing the key conditions before travellers book. When searching for a hire car, the first thing travellers often look at is the headline price. But the lowest value doesn’t always mean the best and usually only covers the basics, with extra costs such as fuel policy, security deposit, insurance, fees for particular pick-up locations, and optional extras such as child seats or additional drivers. Decisions made at the desk are rarely the most cost-effective ones, which is why understanding the full price before booking makes such a difference.

The Indian stock market has been going through a phase that can feel frustrating for investors. The Nifty has spent roughly two years without delivering a positive price return, and after the recent sell-off, the benchmark is actually well below its September 2024 levels. The Nifty closed at 22,620.35 on September 30, 2026, after falling 6.1% in September alone. Compared with levels around 25,800 in late September 2024, the index is down roughly 12% over the two-year period. So, how long can a stock market go without making money? The answer from global market history is: much longer than most investors expect. A two-year period of poor or negative returns can feel unusually long in a market such as India, where investors have seen strong equity returns over the past decade. But, markets do not move in a straight line. There have been several instances when major global indices spent many years recovering from an earlier boom, valuation excess or economic shock. The S&P 500, for instance, went through a prolonged period of weak performance after the dot-com bubble burst. items.text: This Phone Setting Could Save Your Life: How To Set Up Emergency SOS And Medical ID
items.article: Set up Emergency SOS and Medical ID on your Android phone or iPhone so it can call for help, alert family and show your medical details in an emergency. In an accident or medical emergency, the people helping you may not know your blood group, allergies or whom to call. Your smartphone can share all of this, even when it is locked, and can call for help with just a few button presses. These features are built into both Android phones and iPhones, but most people never set them up. It takes about five minutes. Medical ID stores details such as your blood group, allergies, medical conditions, medications and emergency contacts. Anyone can view it from your lock screen without unlocking the phone. Emergency SOS lets you call emergency services quickly using the phone’s buttons. Once the call ends, your phone can also alert your emergency contacts and share your location with them. Go to Settings, then Emergency SOS. Turn on Call with Hold and Release and Call with 5 Button Presses. In an emergency, press and hold the side button with either volume button, or press the side button five times quickly, to start a countdown and call emergency services. Emergency contacts added in your Medical ID will receive a message with your location. On Google Pixel phones, go to Settings, then Safety and emergency. On Samsung phones, go to Settings, then Safety and emergency. On other Android phones, the option is usually under Settings, then Safety or Emergency.

items.article: Could Eli Lilly’s experimental drug be more powerful than Ozempic? Retatrutide has shown up to 28% weight loss in trials, but what does the research actually show? Eli Lilly’s experimental weight-loss drug retatrutide, nicknamed the “Godzilla" of obesity treatments, has delivered striking results in late-stage trials. In people with obesity or overweight, the highest dose produced average weight loss of more than 28% over 80 weeks, roughly twice the typical results seen with semaglutide (the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy) in earlier obesity studies. The findings have generated significant interest because retatrutide works differently from current GLP-1 drugs. While Ozempic primarily targets one hormone pathway, this next-generation candidate activates three. Retatrutide is not yet approved for public use, and there has been no head-to-head trial directly comparing it with Ozempic. Retatrutide is a once-weekly investigational injection that targets three hormone pathways: GLP-1, GIP and glucagon. This is why it is often referred to as a triple agonist. Ozempic, meanwhile, contains semaglutide, which activates the GLP-1 receptor. GLP-1-based medicines can help regulate blood sugar and appetite, while retatrutide is designed to act on an additional GIP pathway and the glucagon receptor, which is involved in energy expenditure and metabolism. They face off in court in a divorce case involving tech entrepreneur Morgan ( Dominic West ) and his film star wife, Carla ( Sienna Miller ). Archie Renaux ‘s character , Johnny, meanwhile is an ambitious young lawyer who is trying to find a job after moving from New York. items.article: Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh says BrahMos is a benchmark for India’s emerging export story, with exports to cross $600 million. Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh hailed BrahMos as a benchmark for India’s emerging export story, with exports expected to cross $600 million. In an interview with ANI on Thursday, Singh said the system has been proven in battle during Operation Sindoor and has an air-launched version. “The system has been proven in battle during Operation Sindoor ...This missile also has an air-launched version, which exists and is a great success on Sukhois," Singh said. He said this is one of the high-end strategic systems that we've been able to export. "There is tremendous potential for this particular system, and I hope that this will continue to be one of the anchors of our export momentum...,” he added. Singh said there are contracts or agreements to sell the high-end strategic system to three Southeast Asian countries — the Philippines, Indonesia and Vietnam. "We've got contracts or agreements to sell it to three Southeast Asian countries, starting with the Philippines, and now Indonesia and Vietnam as well," he told ANI . The BrahMos missile system, to the tune of about $330 million, has been delivered to the Philippines. The Defence Secretary said that exports should be about $100 million to start with for Vietnam, and for Indonesia, it should be around $200 million.

items.text: Explained: Why didn't Christa Pike die despite two lethal injections? The first such case in 207 years
items.article: Christa Pike's execution in Tennessee was unsuccessful after she received two doses of pentobarbital. Despite being strapped to a gurney, she remained alive, eventually being hospitalised. Christa Pike was scheduled to be executed in Tennessee on Wednesday evening but remained alive after two injections of pentobarbital, breathing, making snoring sounds and only complaining that her arm hurt. Pike, sentenced to death for torturing and killing 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995, had said she was at peace as the lethal injection began. Pike, now 50, was 18 when she committed the murder. She would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Instead, she left prison in an ambulance, not a hearse. Here’s what happened during the botched execution and why Pike did not die. The Associated Press witnessed the failed execution. Pike was already strapped to the gurney, with an IV inserted in her arm, when prison officials raised the curtain to the execution room at 7:27 p.m. Minutes passed. Pike raised her head, looked around and smiled. Then she said her arm was hurting and asked a prison official whether it was supposed to feel that way.
